correctness.rationale: A fixed-point-free involution exchanges matching assignments for repeated divisor or target prime-support neighborhoods; when n is squarefree and target supports exhaust all subsets, decreasing-support induction forces exactly one complement matching. An AP can realize half multiples of every prime only with at most two prime factors; two-prime case forces 2 and 3 and exact congruences. Finite exact independent gcd-DP verified 12,320 triples; unrestricted proof does not depend on enumeration.

value.rationale: The natural multiplicity refinement of divisor-set matchability has an exact universal parity/rigidity theorem, a complete classification against every arithmetic progression, a sharp exceptional composite n=6, and an exact answer n=1,2 for the original initial interval. These results distinguish forced arithmetic assignments from mere existence and exclude every squarefree n with at least three prime factors. The count for positive even multiplicities is not determined.
